#9 DURABLE AUTHORITY IDENTITY / PERMIT OWNERSHIP CERTIFICATION (audited head 5b80cbc): correctives #7/#8's linearization points proved authorize-vs-cancel ORDERING was a durable Postgres fact, but neither proved the session row being locked FOR UPDATE was actually the authorized turn's OWN parent session -- AgentService._assert_turn_authority checked turn-terminality and execution_owner_id but never turn.session_id == session_id. Within one Organization, RLS does not help (both a caller-supplied session and a turn's real parent session belong to the same tenant). BLOCKER A fail-first genuinely reproduced against 5b80cbc: session A live/unrelated, turn B's real parent session B already CANCELLED, session_id=A/turn_id=B/owner=B's real owner wrongly authorized a durable permit. FIX: _assert_turn_authority gained an expected_session_id parameter, rejecting (AgentInvalidStateError, existing taxonomy, no new public error code) the moment turn_row.session_id != expected_session_id, inside the SAME FOR UPDATE transaction. Database-level backstop (migration b4c5d6e7f8a9, 'Do NOT rely only on Python'): ai_agent_turns gained an additive unique constraint (organization_id, session_id, id) (existing org+id constraint preserved); ai_agent_tool_dispatch_permits, ai_agent_model_dispatch_permits, AND ai_agent_tool_calls (the audit record of an authorized dispatch's effect) all moved their turn_id FK to the composite (organization_id, session_id, turn_id) -> ai_agent_turns(organization_id, session_id, id) -- proven independent of any application code path by a direct-SQL INSERT test through the tenant-scoped runtime transaction, entirely bypassing AgentService. INV-AUTH-ID-001. BLOCKER B: a SAVEPOINT + contextlib.suppress(IntegrityError) pattern made 'I created the permit' indistinguishable from 'one already existed' -- safe for tool dispatch (P08's own idempotency key backstops a second attempt) but unsafe for model dispatch specifically (no backstop against a second real, billed provider call). FIX: a new internal-only _PermitOutcome enum (CREATED/ALREADY_EXISTS) makes the branch explicit; model dispatch now REJECTS ALREADY_EXISTS, tool dispatch deliberately keeps proceeding on it (documented P08-idempotency rationale). Public AuthorizeModel/AuthorizeTool callback contracts in runtime.py UNCHANGED. INV-AUTH-ID-002. Table audit: exactly 3 P13 tables carry both session_id+turn_id, all 3 fixed; ai_model_usage (session_id only) correctly out of scope. NXS-AGENT-002 left completely UNCHANGED (still mandatory=true/PLANNED/NXS-P25) -- verified byte-identical to corrective #8's close. 20 new tests (fail-first proofs, mandatory model+tool duplicate-permit tests, full 7-row wrong-owner/wrong-session matrix for both model and tool, direct-SQL DB-constraint proof). TEST-ROBUSTNESS FIX (found and fixed, not a production defect, while re-verifying zero regression per directive requirement): two PRE-EXISTING single-worker tests in test_agent_concurrency.py (test_model_response_racing_a_cancellation_leaves_no_stale_answer, test_stop_during_a_turn_terminalizes_and_rejects_further_turns) intermittently failed under full-suite load with 'DID NOT RAISE' -- root cause: a fixed asyncio.sleep(0.1) is not sufficient proof that submit_turn has registered the _run_turn task in self._turn_tasks (an intervening `await self.get_agent(...)` sits between _open_turn's commit and that registration), so the terminalize fast-path finds no task to cancel and the model call completes undisturbed. Fixed by waiting for the durable model-dispatch permit to exist instead -- provably race-free. Ruled out (and confirmed via direct code reading) that the SAME race affects test_agent_tool_dispatch_fencing.py / test_agent_model_dispatch_fencing.py's own sleep(0.1) usages: those tests use TWO independent AgentService instances, so the cancelling worker's own self._turn_tasks never has an entry for the OTHER worker's task -- their correctness already rests entirely on the DB-level session-row FOR UPDATE lock, never exposed to this race. A follow-up commit also widened 3 turn-lookup indexes (ix_ai_agent_tool_dispatch_permits_turn, ix_ai_agent_model_dispatch_permits_turn, ix_ai_agent_tool_calls_turn) to lead with session_id, matching the new composite FK column order (independent-audit LOW finding, addressed before closure). Adversarial validation: independent red-team subagent GO (zero findings after 40 tool uses of live verification: full diff read, both authorize-method call sites confirmed as the only two, live migration up/down/up/check cycle, all 20 new tests run live, 115+124-test regression runs, cross-tenant isolation confirmed, ai_agent_tool_calls insert-site safety confirmed, runtime.py contract confirmed unchanged, ruff/mypy/schema-guard clean, zero .nxs/ governance diff). Independent final-auditor subagent GO (zero BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM, one non-blocking LOW addressed, after 68 tool uses: independently REPRODUCED the fail-first vulnerability against the actual pre-fix commit 5b80cbc + pre-fix schema in a scratch git worktree with a downgraded database -- not merely re-stating the diff -- live migration cycle, full 1549-test suite run with zero failures, full static validation, governance-diff confirmation).
